A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dota, and their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched despite substantial revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Dota classification results, human-feedback experiments, timing measurements and ablations, including the ImageNet-V2 analysis in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original Dota benchmark results, pathology evaluations, ablations, and appendix experiments on different data orderings and non-i.i.d. streams.

M1.justification: v2 removes v1's uncertainty-based sample selection and human-feedback adaptation component, including its steps in Algorithm 1. It also changes initialization from class text embeddings to a constant vector, and the initial effective sample count from 1 to 0 (Sections 3.2–3.3). The Gaussian estimation and adaptive logit-fusion framework remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds pathology classification on Kather, PanNuke and WSSS4LUAD, plus deliberately non-i.i.d. ImageNet streams. Human-feedback evaluation scenarios disappear. The original natural-image datasets remain represented; ImageNet-V2 was already evaluated in v1's appendix and is not new coverage.

E2.justification: The cross-domain comparison adds BoostAdapter, HisTPT, ZERO and a prompt-enhanced DMN comparison; the natural-shift comparison adds ZERO. v2 also adds TDA to the overall-versus-last-half analysis, previously containing only Dota. Random and similarity-based feedback-selection comparisons disappear with the feedback experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds PLIP and prompt-enhanced evaluation configurations while removing ResNet-50 from the main cross-domain and natural-shift comparisons, retaining it for ImageNet-V2. Appendix A.3 introduces Dirichlet-generated streams with 5 or 10 slices, concentration parameters 0.1, 0.5 and 1, and sample-weighted accuracy. These substantially revise the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds high-confidence pseudo-label ablation, hyperparameter and fusion analyses, ordering robustness, and non-i.i.d. stream tests (Table 7–11). It expands the last-half analysis with TDA but removes EuroSAT there. v1's feedback-selection and selected-sample accuracy analyses disappear. The ImageNet-V2 failure analysis is retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 does not document repeated-order evaluations. v2 Appendix A.2 reports five ordering-specific outcomes and their averages for ImageNet, EuroSAT and OxfordPets. This adds limited evidence about variability without establishing an increase over v1's actual run count; seeds, confidence intervals and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Reported ViT-B/16 Dota averages change from 69.01 to 69.71 across domains and from 66.09 to 66.31 under natural shifts. ImageNet-V2 and covariance-ablation values also change. v2 adds pathology, prompt-enhancement and robustness results while removing feedback and most ResNet-50 entries. These revisions accompany changed initialization and should not be interpreted as gains from an unchanged procedure.

T1.justification: v2 formalizes the existing EM interpretation as Proposition 3.1 and adds a likelihood-based derivation of the weighted Gaussian estimators in Appendix A.1. The Gaussian and uniform-prior assumptions already existed in v1. It also adds a cited vanishing-average-regret statement and removes the feedback uncertainty definition. The theoretical expansion chiefly supports existing estimators.

C1.justification: v1 presents a novel human-feedback TTA task as a principal contribution in its abstract, introduction and conclusion. v2 withdraws that contribution and centers the paper on automatic distributional adaptation and mitigation of forgetting across cache-based methods. The central distribution-estimation and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning soft probabilities versus high-confidence pseudo-labels, adaptive fusion, limited hyperparameter sensitivity, and robustness to ordering and non-i.i.d. streams. Feedback-related interpretations and future directions disappear. The limited-sample explanation for ImageNet-V2 is largely retained and made more prominent, rather than constituting a new limitation.

D1.justification: The original batch size, hyperparameter search grids and hardware remain documented. v2 adds the initialization value omega = 0.0001, pathology prompt examples and dataset sizes, and stream-construction details. It promises code release without providing access. The natural-shift tuning description loses v1's explicit identification of the single ImageNet validation set.

R1.justification: v2 removes the uncertainty-estimation literature discussion and adds substantial positioning around distribution estimation, prototype learning and continual recognition. It introduces discussion of T3A, RoTTA, universal TTA and BoostAdapter, alongside newer comparison-method citations. This changes the research context beyond citation formatting or publication updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work is regrouped, the human-feedback section disappears, the two main benchmark discussions exchange order, and the appendix gains named subsections. The author block, acknowledgments and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a cache-versus-distribution diagram and removes the human-feedback pipeline. v1 Figure 1 survives as v2 Figure 2, while Figure 3 loses its feedback curves. Tables are extensively restructured, including rotated dataset headings and new analysis tables; the ImageNet-V2 table moves into the main text. Algorithm 1 changes from a wrapped display to full width.

improvement.justification: Newer comparators and targeted ablation and stream-robustness experiments strengthen support for the retained automatic adapter, addressing questions v1 did not test. The existing ImageNet-V2 limitation is also more visible. These benefits accompany narrower feedback and backbone coverage. Reporting problems limit the improvement: v2 Table 1 contradicts the retained claim of top-two performance on every dataset, and the pathology class counts conflict between Section 4 and Table 12.
